title: Suspicious-word check matches case-insensitively and ignores surrounding whitespace
description: profile/page.jsx's handleSaveProfile() builds isInvalid(v) as SUSPICIOUS_WORDS.has(v.trim().toLowerCase()) against a fixed Set (test, admin, dummy, sample, demo, fake, example, default, placeholder, etc.). Verifies the trim+lowercase normalisation actually catches padded/mixed-case variants, not just exact lowercase matches.
preconditions: isInvalid()/SUSPICIOUS_WORDS logic extracted or tested in isolation from ProfilePage
expectedResult: All three calls return true — whitespace padding and casing do not defeat the suspicious-word check.

title: Suspicious-word check is exact-match, not substring — legitimate names containing a banned word are not flagged
description: isInvalid() uses SUSPICIOUS_WORDS.has(v.trim().toLowerCase()), a Set membership test against the whole trimmed value — not a .includes()/regex substring test. A name like 'Newton' (contains 'new') or 'Sampson' (contains 'sample'... no, contains 'samp') must not be rejected just because a banned word appears as a substring.
expectedResult: All three calls return false — the check only rejects the banned words as complete values, never as substrings of a longer legitimate name.

title: getUserDisplayName() falls back through fullName -> firstName+lastName -> name -> email in priority order
description: profile/page.jsx's getUserDisplayName(u): returns u.fullName if present, else `${firstName} ${lastName}`.trim() if either is present, else u.name, else u.email, else ''.
steps: Call getUserDisplayName({ fullName: 'A B', firstName: 'X', email: 'x@y.com' }) — expect 'A B'
Call getUserDisplayName({ firstName: 'Jane', lastName: 'Doe', email: 'j@d.com' }) — expect 'Jane Doe'
Call getUserDisplayName({ name: 'Legacy Name', email: 'l@n.com' }) — expect 'Legacy Name'
expectedResult: Each call returns exactly the value from the highest-priority source available, matching the documented fallback order.

title: getDepartmentName() handles a populated department object, a plain string, and an absent field
description: profile/page.jsx's getDepartmentName(u): returns '' if !u?.department, u.department.name if department is an object, otherwise the raw string value.
expectedResult: All three cases return the documented value with no thrown error.

title: updateMe's conditional $set construction skips an empty-string firstName/lastName rather than clearing it
description: user.controller.js exports.updateMe builds its Mongo $set with `...(firstName && { firstName })` — a spread guarded by JS truthiness, so an empty string '' (falsy) is silently omitted from the update instead of clearing the stored name. This is a controller-level safety net independent of any frontend validation, and should be covered directly against the update-object-building logic.
preconditions: updateMe's $set-building logic tested with a mocked User.findByIdAndUpdate, or the update object construction extracted for direct unit testing
steps: Invoke the update-object builder with firstName: '' and lastName: 'Smith'
expectedResult: The $set payload contains lastName: 'Smith' but does NOT contain a firstName key at all — an empty string never reaches the database as a cleared value.

title: changeOwnPassword rejects when newPassword equals oldPassword before any Keycloak call is made
description: user.controller.js exports.changeOwnPassword checks `if (newPassword === oldPassword) throw AppError.badRequest(...)` as its very first statement, ahead of the User lookup and the verifyUserPassword() Keycloak ROPC call — so this guard is cheap and short-circuits before any network I/O.
preconditions: verifyUserPassword and setUserPassword mocked so the test can assert they were never invoked
steps: Assert the thrown error and that verifyUserPassword/setUserPassword were never called
expectedResult: A 400 AppError 'New password must be different from the current password' is thrown, and no Keycloak API calls occur.
